title: Prove additive-frame requirements for unchanged scalar gates (no new κ)
body:
The coherent-frame route left open by PR4966 also needs scalar-gate compatibility. A shared potential commuting with an unchanged dyadic-unit ADD on arbitrary inputs must be additive. The independent source audit finds such an ADD on **every one of the 1,002 active frames in each retained round-three orientation**.

The package includes a written proof, exact reversible nonlinear and unitary-equivariant counterexamples, 2,004 source-event witnesses, and the paid graph's 2,297 fundamental closed-walk tests per orientation. Those cycle counts identify obligations; they do not show failures of a particular realization. This is a boundary theorem for the gatewise coherent-potential recipe, not a general exclusion of correlated-error implementations or a new κ.

Yiyang (@Lyy-iiis) supplies PR4966's same-realization inverse construction and independent-error precision census; Cao Yifan supplies the actual round-three word and its retained predecessor lineage. Nick Petalas's related binary symplectic graph transport work is credited. The exact pending predecessor proof is vendored with commit/blob/SHA256 pins; the scientific replay imports no predecessor implementation.

Validation on Python 3.12.3:

- Isolated normal and optimized source/certificate replays pass, including frame chronology, both persistent endpoint lists, owned-center macro separation, all frame witnesses and five specified rejection controls.
- Registered package replay passes with outcome=completed; metadata/source pins and committed-byte/source-history preflight pass.
- Canonical main and live open-PR/discussion overlap refreshed before publication. No selected cold replay, native physical suite, Lean build or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

The remaining task is an additive, fully priced coherent realization, or a changed scalar/caller argument with its own complete bill. See `research/coherent-frame-additivity/PROOF.md` and its Open next questions. Canonical investigation: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4611#discussioncomment-19138553.

Prepared by Cinna Davis with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in research, proof explanation, implementation, verification and writing. No independent human review claimed. Apache-2.0.
